budget_items.what_was_recorded: Public speaker reported that Ashby taxpayers agreed to pay a figure in one fiscal year for projects funded by short-term borrowing and debt exclusions.
budget_items.quote: the ashby taxpayer has agreed to pay $634.85 in one fiscal year to accomplish the projects.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Public speaker cited the share of town spending going to schools and police.

budget_items.topic: Unfunded health and retirement and OPEB obligation
budget_items.what_was_recorded: Public speaker commented on a $100K amount for unfunded health and retirement against a total OPEB obligation.
budget_items.quote: commented on the $100k for the unfunded health and retirement versus the total large obligation of about $35m for opeb.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Public comment referenced a school budget increase of about $1M a year, attributed to a Selectmen comment at a previous meeting.
budget_items.quote: dave referenced a comment from selectmen luck at a previous meeting about the school budget going up about $1m a year.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Discussion that the school committee asked for a 9% increase and the Finance Committee approved 5.5%, with concern that revenues grow only about 3%.
budget_items.quote: previously the school committee had asked for 9% budget increase and we approved 5.5%.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Clarification that the $1M figure is the approximate total cost of the new teachers contract over three years, salary increases only.
budget_items.quote: that figure is the approximate total cost of the new teachers contract over the next 3 years.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Town Manager/Financial officer reported real estate taxes are usually collected at a percentage.
budget_items.quote: real estate taxes are usually at 98%.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Explanation that the levy base can increase 2.5% a year and an override is needed to go above that.
budget_items.quote: the base can only increase 2.5%. an override is needed to raise taxes over the 2.5%.
